issues.issue: Audited earned premium may exceed the advance premium stated in the Declarations, which sits uneasily with the Non-Assessable condition (c046) promising the insured is not liable for any premium other than that stated in the policy.
It requires only 30 days' notice of nonrenewal, while the Kansas Changes Nonrenewal provision (c249) requires 60 days' notice stating reasons for this policy.
"'Bodily injury' means bodily injury, sickness or disease" defines the term by repeating it, leaving whether purely emotional injury is included unresolved.
"[O]ne which becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be" gives no test for when a fire that was never "intended" at all is hostile.

Limb f. is a general catch-all — "that part of any other contract or agreement pertaining to your business ... under which you assume the tort liability of another" — sitting after five narrowly enumerated agreement types, leaving its reach open to an ejusdem generis argument.
"'Occurrence' means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions" defines the term by an undefined word, "accident".

Limb c. covers "wrongful eviction from, wrongful entry into, or invasion of the right of private occupancy of a room, dwelling or premises" committed by or on behalf of "its owner, landlord or lessor", and the boundary of "invasion of the right of private occupancy" is not fixed.

The closing paragraph is corrupted ("or the purposes of this insurance, electronic dala © ivy not tangible property. s used in this definttion ..."), so the electronic-data carve-out cannot be read as written.
The "Your product" definition runs into the separate "Your work" definition mid-paragraph, so limbs b. and c. of each are interleaved and neither definition is complete.

The enumeration is corrupted ("a Any supervision" for item 5 and "&. Any obligation" for item 6), so the cross-references to "parts 1. through 4." and "parts 1. through 5." do not line up with the list.
The Coverage A and Coverage B versions of the exclusion have run together into a single interleaved block, so the exclusion added to Coverage A cannot be read apart from the Coverage B text.

This entry reproduces the same interleaved Coverage A/Coverage B text as the preceding provision and then repeats the "This exclusion applies" paragraph, so the same words appear twice as separate provisions.
The Coverage A and Coverage B limbs are interleaved and the Coverage B text is corrupted ("'Personai would nob place ... afigi' or bacterla"), so neither exclusion reads as a complete sentence.

The provision is captioned as the Coverage B exclusion but its opening words add the exclusion to "Section I — Coverage A — Bodily Injury And Property Damage Liability", and the body duplicates the preceding entry.

The lead-in "[t]he following exclusions are added to all coverages contained within" does not identify what is contained within, and sub-items c. and d. of paragraph 3 are supervision and indemnity limbs that do not fit the "any loss, cost or expense arising out of any" stem.

"[A]ny injury or damage" is defined as any injury or damage covered under any Coverage Part and "includes but is not limited to" a list of defined terms, an open catch-all whose outer limit is not stated.
The opening words are scrambled ("temeecs of an act that her act of terrorism' means a violent act is dangerous to human life"), so the definition's subject is missing.

It replaces Exclusion i. of Coverage A with a broader war exclusion, while the printed Coverage A exclusions (c268) still contain the narrower War exclusion applying "only to liability assumed under a contract or agreement".

It turns off Exclusion h. of Coverage C and relies instead on Exclusion g., but the printed Coverage C exclusions (c274) still contain both, so the war treatment of medical payments has to be reconstructed across two provisions.
